articles.chapeau: Rob Nelson told VGC Rockstar never planned to reveal GTA 6 story detail Tomás and is praying it stays under wraps. What is confirmed so far.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Spoiler note: this story discusses one early plot detail from Grand Theft Auto VI . If you have not reached it yet, stop here and come back later.
Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, told Video Games Chronicle (VGC) that he is “praying it stays under wraps.” The detail in question is the early story reveal that Jason and Lucia have a son named Tomás. Reports dated November 26, 2026 say Rockstar never planned to reveal it before launch, and Nelson’s own words back that up.
The comments land in a strange news cycle. GTA 6 went on sale on November 19, 2026, and the conversation since then has been dominated by sales, leaks and legal fights. Our own coverage of the post-launch period and the missing roadmap showed how much attention the game still pulls. Nelson’s plea adds a different thread: a studio leader asking an enormous audience to leave one story beat alone.

VGC interviewed Nelson, and the exchange was picked up by IGN, IGN Southeast Asia and Beebom. All of them focused on the same two points. First, the game’s early story establishes that Jason and Lucia have a son named Tomás. Second, Rockstar had no intention of putting that fact into marketing before players reached it themselves.
That second point is the real news. Big publishers usually push their strongest story material into trailers, because trailers drive pre-orders. Rockstar did the opposite with this beat. Nelson’s answer to the question of whether the studio would ever have revealed it was blunt, and the reports quote him saying no.
The reports describe the reveal as part of the early-game or prologue context. They do not describe how the scene plays out, what the character’s role is later, or how the story builds on it. We are keeping to the same limit. Anything past the single fact that Tomás exists, and that Rockstar held it back, would be guesswork, and this article does not guess.
Nelson’s title matters too. As co-studio head at Rockstar North, he speaks for the team that builds the game, not for a marketing department. A marketing executive saying “we kept it secret” is a strategy statement. A studio head saying he is praying it stays secret is closer to an emotional one, and it tells readers how much the team cares about the first-play experience.
Three direct statements from Nelson appear in the reporting. We reproduce them exactly as they were published, with VGC as the interview source.
The bracketed words come from the published reports, which means the sentence answers a question about revealing the detail. It settles the debate about whether Rockstar held a secret trailer moment in reserve. According to Nelson, no such moment existed.
“I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps.”
This is the line that gave the story its headline. It reads like a person counting down to something, though the reports we reviewed do not say what the countdown refers to. We flag that gap again below, because it affects how readers should place the quote on the calendar.
“Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'”
The phrase “everything that we’ve gone through” is worth a pause. Nelson does not list what he means, and the reports do not either. Readers who followed the leak stories can fill in context, but the sheet of confirmed facts does not tie his words to any specific incident. We treat the line as a general reference to a hard stretch for the studio.

articles.t: GTA 6 tourne « mieux » sur un BC-250 que sur PS5
articles.chapeau: AMD a vendu les cartes BC-250, aux caractéristiques techniques revues à la baisse par rapport à celles d’une PS5, pour servir de systèmes de minage de cryptomonnaies. Quelqu’un a maintenant modifié le matériel pour l’utiliser comme une PS5 et y faire tourner GTA 6.
articles.txt:
Malgré les efforts de Take-Two pour freiner les portages non officiels sur PC de GTA 6 , on a l’impression que les choses avancent d’heure en heure. À ce rythme, ce n’est plus qu’une question de jours avant que GTA 6 soit entièrement jouable sur PC . Mais la communauté ne s’arrête pas au PC : du matériel de PS5 réaffecté ferait apparemment mieux tourner le jeu que le matériel officiel.
La carte BC-250 d’AMD embarque une version allégée de l’APU de la PS5, avec les mêmes 16 Go de mémoire GDDR6 et un bus de 256 bits. Elle repose sur la même architecture CPU Zen 2 et la même architecture GPU RDNA 2. En revanche, le nombre de cœurs, de threads, d’unités de calcul (CU) et de processeurs de flux a été réduit, tout comme les fréquences d’horloge. Cela aurait permis à AMD de reconvertir ces cartes en matériel de minage de cryptomonnaies et de les vendre à ASRock.
Avec le déclin du minage de cryptomonnaies, ces cartes ont été vendues au grand public et ont depuis été réaffectées, une fois de plus, à divers usages. On les trouve en ligne entre 120 et 250 dollars, ce qui les rend nettement moins chères qu’une PS5 standard. De plus, des moddeurs sont parvenus à débrider ces cartes, permettant à la BC-250 d’égaler les performances de la PS5, voire de les dépasser dans certains cas.
Un internaute du nom de « djaye », qui se décrit comme un « adepte de la rétro-ingénierie pour le jeu de rôle », est parvenu à faire tourner GTA 6 sur ce qui semble être une BC-250 overclockée ou débridée, à 35 images par seconde (FPS), du moins à en juger par la capture d’écran publiée sur X. On y voit Lucia en prison et, en haut, des statistiques de performances indiquant 35 FPS, avec des creux à 29 FPS. Même si une seule capture d’écran ne permet pas vraiment de comparer en temps réel les performances avec celles de la PS5 standard , ces chiffres semblent prometteurs.
Le moddeur utilise la version 25.06-12.00.00 du micrologiciel, qui date d’un peu plus d’un an. On ne sait pas s’il compte optimiser davantage le matériel, quels outils il a utilisés pour le modifier, ni s’il prévoit de publier des séquences de jeu. Quoi qu’il en soit, il est intéressant de voir qu’une carte initialement basée sur une PS5, puis reconvertie pour le minage de cryptomonnaies, sert désormais de PS5 et fait tourner GTA 6 un peu mieux que la PS5 officielle.

articles.txt:
Share Save Add as preferred on Google Laura Cress Technology reporter Rockstar Games / Take-Two Interactive Grand Theft Auto 6 saw record retail sales in its first full day of release, hitting $3.8bn (£2.9bn), making it the biggest entertainment launch in history Hot off its record-breaking console launch, the developer of Grand Theft Auto 6 is facing a problem – and it's one that is increasingly affecting the wider games industry.
Rockstar is yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6, but with the emergence of powerful AI tools, coders and gamers have taken matters into their own hands.
The developer has typically released Grand Theft Auto on PC long after its initial console launch – 19 months later in the case of GTA 5.
This time it may not have that luxury – in part because of an apparent leak of files from an Xbox development build of the game, but also due to the rapid advance of AI coding platforms.
These tools are being used to recreate or adapt existing games, sometimes within days, taking away the control developers have over their products.
Barely a week after the release of GTA 6, efforts are already under way to get an unofficial version playable on PC, although some projects have faced takedown notices from the game's publisher.
For some gamers, it's an exciting prospect, despite the legal questions surrounding the process.
For developers, it may be a warning: if a game as big as GTA 6 can be recreated, what does that mean for everyone else?
The recent wave of AI-assisted game recreation has been widely linked to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 model, released in September, and to agentic tools such as Claude Code.
Mark Brown, creator of the YouTube channel Game Maker's Toolkit and whose own game Word Play was recently recreated using AI, said cloning largely took two forms: replication and reverse engineering.
Replication is where someone asks an AI chatbot such as Claude or ChatGPT to build a new game based on an existing one, possibly using screenshots or a description.
This, he said, was similar to "looking at a painting and making your own replica" – something which is "a very close copy, but is ultimately a new painting".
It's a particular issue among smaller studios, many of whom worry that AI makes it easier for others to copy their work.
When indie developers Sodoj and Marco from the studio Robotonic noticed a version of their unreleased puzzle game 204Snake appear on the free games platform Yandex with the same name, they were "appalled".
"The game was essentially the exact same idea, the exact same mechanics as we had, but with the art looking a bit off," Marco told the BBC .
The duo were able to issue a copyright strike to Yandex and Google to get the copy taken down, but said it only felt like a "small victory".
The second approach – reverse engineering – involves working backwards from a finished game to understand how it was created.
One way of doing this is decompilation, which attempts to turn the game's final version into something closer to its original source code.
Brown compares the process to "taking a cake and somehow turning it back into the original recipe, with the exact quantities of flour, eggs, and milk used, so anyone can remake the same cake".
Reverse-engineering projects have helped bring games such as Halo: Combat Evolved and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City to web browsers.
A related technique, recompilation, can help adapt a game that has been reverse-engineered to run on different hardware. This is one of the methods being explored in efforts to get GTA 6 onto PC.
Coders wanting to attempt this with Rockstar's latest game face a difficult task because of its sheer size and complexity.
Earlier in November, Cyberleek – a hacker or group of hackers – released what they claimed to be a near-complete Xbox development build of the game. They later leaked what they claimed to be the missing .exe file needed to launch the game.
It gave those working on an unofficial PC version a crucial new starting point.
"Now people are using AI to try and decompile it, make a modified version that could run on PC, and compile a new version," said Brown.
Since the leak, several groups have posted claims of their progress on platforms such as X, ranging from getting the game to boot up to making it run at a stable rate.
One attempt seen by the BBC on X purported to have some of the game running nearly as smoothly as it does on console, albeit on a high-end PC.

articles.t: Rockstar écoule 53 millions de GTA VI en une semaine, les autres jeux sous pression
articles.chapeau: GTA VI dépasserait 53 millions de ventes en une semaine, dont 75,7 % sur PS5. Alinea Analytics mesure aussi un recul des revenus des autres jeux premium.
articles.txt:
Environ 250 000 joueurs auraient déjà passé plus de 100 heures dans le nouveau monde ouvert de Rockstar en sept jours. Cette mobilisation se retrouve dans les estimations commerciales, mais aussi dans les revenus des jeux concurrents, en recul sur la période.
Après près de 45 millions d’exemplaires écoulés à la fin du week-end de lancement, GTA VI aurait dépassé les 53 millions de ventes sur sa première semaine , d’après les estimations d’Alinea Analytics. Le rythme a ralenti après les premiers jours, tout en restant suffisamment soutenu pour franchir largement le seuil des 50 millions sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series.
La répartition entre les deux plateformes est particulièrement déséquilibrée : la famille PS5 représenterait 75,7 % des ventes , soit environ 40 millions d’exemplaires. Les consoles Xbox totaliseraient, elles, quelque 13 millions de copies.
Alinea évalue les revenus générés à 4,7 milliards de dollars. À cette échelle commerciale s’ajoute une consommation intensive chez une partie du public : dépasser 100 heures de jeu en une semaine, comme l’auraient fait environ 250 000 joueurs, représente plus de 14 heures quotidiennes.
Plusieurs studios avaient déplacé leurs sorties après l’annonce de la date de lancement du jeu de Rockstar, par crainte de voir leurs ventes pénalisées. Alinea a examiné cette hypothèse en suivant les tendances commerciales de 11 jeux premium sur PlayStation.
L’échantillon comprend 007 First Light, Phantom Blade Zero, Wolverine, Crimson Desert, The Blood of Dawnwalker, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced, Ghost of Yōtei, Star Wars Galactic Racer, Onimusha Way of the Sword, Resident Evil Requiem et Gran Turismo 7.
Sur ce périmètre, les revenus auraient baissé jusqu’à 24 % pendant la semaine suivant le lancement . La comparaison a toutefois une limite importante : certains titres étaient sortis plusieurs mois auparavant et suivaient déjà une trajectoire descendante. Le recul observé ne peut donc pas être intégralement attribué à GTA VI.
Pour les éditeurs concurrents, le risque ne se limite pas au budget consacré à l’achat : le temps disponible devient lui aussi une contrainte. Décaler une sortie peut éviter la confrontation immédiate, sans garantir de retrouver rapidement un public disponible pour un autre jeu.

GTA 6 PS5 and PS5 Pro players note downgraded graphics following first update
articles.chapeau: The initial GTA 6 update did not list performance changes in its patch notes. Regardless, some PS5 Pro and PS5 players believe object detail and lighting suffered in version 01.002.002. With demanding graphics, Rockstar may be aim to lighten the load imposed on consoles.
articles.txt:
Rockstar distributed the first post-release date GTA 6 update on November 23rd. Version 01.002.002 targeted crashes , static weather , and other issues. However, some PS5 and PS5 Pro console owners have described reduced image quality. Gamers speculate that developers downgraded the graphics to improve performance .
While not every poster agrees, Reddit has seen a rise in threads about lower-quality visuals. Players have noted blurry textures, increased pop-in, and less convincing global illumination.
Redditor Dem5869 says after the update, “lighting, textures, and hair look completely different…” Many observations relate to dynamic weather in the GTA 6 PS5 Pro version. Sunrises and sunsets now lack the wow factor they had on release date. Clouds seem pixelated, and the water reflections left by rainstorms disappoint.
DrGonzoRoyale echoes those thoughts, adding that a more aggressive depth of field makes distant objects blurry. The facial features and hair strands of Jason , Lucia , and NPCs are also less defined. The poster claims screenshots prove the differences aren't just imagined.
Although the PS5 Pro enhancements boost performance, Digital Foundry recorded frame rate drops in crowded scenes. Despite the 30 fps cap, the Rockstar title stresses Xbox and PlayStation consoles, which may contribute to overheating reports . A cutback in visual fidelity would ease the strain on the gaming machines.
Perhaps because the GTA 6 PS5 Pro upgrade renders the most detailed Leonida , the issues are most noticeable on this hardware. Some players suspect the PSSR 2 implementation has seen changes. If the upscaling isn’t as effective, that could explain why objects are no longer as sharp.
Rockstar fans are reminded of the Red Dead Redemption 2 launch on the PS4 Pro and Xbox One . Patch 1.06 produced similar rumblings about less authentic lighting and shadows. Still, version 1.09 then introduced HDR refinements, largely eliminating many of the complaints.
Until the studio comments on any performance tweaks, it’s wise not to draw conclusions. Digital Foundry and other sites will keep analyzing the graphics as future GTA 6 updates arrive.

articles.t: GTA 6's headphone feature was originally planned for GTA: Vice City back in 2002, former Rockstar developer reveals
articles.chapeau: Former Rockstar tech lead Obbe Vermeij says the studio planned a portable radio for Vice City in 2002, but it was cut for technical reasons.
articles.txt:
Former Rockstar tech lead Obbe Vermeij says a portable radio feature planned for Vice City in 2002 was dropped for an unknown technical reason. GTA 6 now lets players hear radio or podcasts through headphones outside cars, though it does not allow choosing individual tracks.
As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases. TweakTown may also earn commissions from Best Buy and other affiliate partners at no extra cost to you.
GTA 6 is full of small touches that make the world feel real. You can push your car when it runs out of gas, and you can open the door for Lucia. One of those touches is the headphones mechanic. Music used to live in your car radio and stop the moment you got out, but now you can put in a pair of headphones and take it with you.
Turns out, that feature could have been part of GTA more than two decades ago. Former Rockstar tech lead Obbe Vermeij says the studio planned a headphones feature for Vice City in 2002. He posted on X that it "didn't happen for some technical reason I can't remember," and attached the pickup icon the team made for it.
Popular Now: 209GB GTA 6 'PC version' appears on Russian torrent site Vermeij's post was a reply to a viral post praising the headphones in GTA 6 and how much they add to immersion. He worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009, so he was there for Vice City. He doesn't remember why it got cut, so nothing is confirmed, though fans are guessing. He also clarified that it was meant to be a portable radio, rather than a Walkman-style player that would let you pick songs. That's worth noting, since GTA 6 doesn't let you pick your own tracks either.
In GTA 6, you can put in earbuds or headphones and keep listening to the radio or podcasts when you step out of the car, and the game plays nicely with combat and exploration.

articles.t: GTA 6 Chapter 1's Ending Has A Major Twist You Need To Watch Out For - SVG
articles.chapeau: The first chapter of "Grand Theft Auto VI" is functionally a prologue, and that comes complete with a gentle warning about what to prepare for.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "GTA 6"
After waiting years for the release, gamers are now tearing through the "Grand Theft Auto VI" story at full speed. They're fixing up projects at Jason's house and building up a nest egg with a combination of drug trafficking and petty crime. There are unlimited activities to do in "GTA 6," but players who are moving at warp speed through the early game should be aware of a big twist that comes at the end of Chapter 1.
Without getting into spoilers, we'll just say that the ending of Chapter 1 causes players to lose their house, cars, and all of their money. The beginning of the story sets up Jason's connection to Brian Heder and his relationship with Lucia, while it also introduces several important side characters and mechanics that players will be engaging with throughout the game. The acts you take matter, but the "GTA 6" Chapter 1 ending will act as a soft reset and it sends Jason and Lucia on a new, unexpected path. Read on if you want to know what causes the dramatic loss at the end of "GTA 6" Chapter 1 and to find out what bits of player progression survive the purge.
Rockstar Games Jason and Lucia are constantly trying to avoid the police and the dreaded six-star wanted level in "GTA 6," but at the end of Chapter 1, their luck runs out. In the middle of an important and potentially lucrative job, our leads get arrested by undercover cops and pulled into a makeshift interrogation room. While Jason and Lucia are being questioned, Officer Aldo Méndez enters the room, and it immediately becomes apparent he's on a different wavelength than the other cops.
Méndez kills the detective interrogating Jason and Lucia, and tries to kill them. In the process of making their escape, the duo also gets out with a bag containing an encrypted hard drive that Méndez badly wants. Thugs show up at Jason's house and burn the place down, and then Méndez and his loyalists frame the two of them for the murder he committed. Because of that, Jason and Lucia are broke, on the run, and wanted by people on both sides of the law.
Rockstar Games The ending of "GTA 6" Chapter 1 acts like a soft reset. Players lose their home, cars, and money, but they don't lose everything. The actions players take throughout Chapter 1 still matter, and parts of their progress carries over into Chapter 2. The "GTA 6" criminal profile system has a constant effect on the game, so Jason and Lucia will keep the profiles player the helped them develop in Chapter 1. The leads will maintain whatever relationship status they've achieved by the end of the first act of the game, too, so all the early game chores and flirting still matters.
Players wanting to know how to get their stuff back after the "GTA 6" Chapter 1 ending get a small piece of good news. Some things remain at the charred remnants of Jason's house. Players who go back will find that Jason's beloved pet snake survived the blaze, and they'll be able to dig Jason's metal stash box out of the ashes to regain a small amount of cash. Since players can also keep their side quest and collectibles progressions, the "GTA 6" Chapter 1 ending isn't a total loss.

Comme dans GTA V, nos décisions peuvent influencer le dénouement de Grand Theft Auto VI. Mais cette fois, Rockstar Games va beaucoup plus loin puisque la conclusion de l’aventure dépend non seulement des derniers choix du scénario, mais également de notre comportement tout au long du jeu. La relation entre Jason et Lucia, leur profil criminel ou encore leurs économies peuvent ainsi modifier radicalement leur destin. Voici comment débloquer les différentes fins de GTA 6 et obtenir la meilleure conclusion possible.
Attention, spoilers majeurs : ce guide dévoile les événements du chapitre 5, les derniers choix du scénario et le sort des personnages principaux. Nous vous déconseillons de poursuivre votre lecture si vous n’avez pas terminé l’histoire. Vous cherchez plutôt ce qu’il faut faire avant la fin d’un chapitre ? Consultez nos guides sur la fin du chapitre 1 et la fin du chapitre 2 de GTA 6 . Sinon, voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur les fins de GTA VI.
Combien de fins y a-t-il dans GTA 6 ? On peut distinguer huit grands dénouements , auxquels s’ajoutent plusieurs variantes qui modifient certaines cinématiques et scènes après le générique. Ces fins dépendent principalement de quatre éléments :
Il existe deux grands parcours : l’un mène à un affrontement final avec les forces de l’ordre sur un pont, tandis que l’autre se termine au pied de la tour de Giorgio Gallo.
Commençons directement par ce qui intéressera probablement la majorité d’entre vous. La meilleure fin permet à Jason et Lucia de survivre, de retrouver leur liberté et de vivre ensemble avec leur fils Tomás . Cependant, cette conclusion demande plusieurs préparatifs avant de commencer les dernières missions.
Vous devez impérativement atteindre le quatrième et dernier niveau de relation, intitulé « À la vie, à la mort ». Pour cela, multipliez les activités avec votre partenaire : sorties, repas, sports, promenades, braquages en couple et interactions romantiques. Pensez également à répondre à ses messages et à éviter les comportements susceptibles de dégrader votre relation.
Vous pouvez consulter votre niveau actuel depuis le menu consacré à Jason et Lucia. Si vous avez besoin d’aide, consultez notre guide pour augmenter la relation entre Jason et Lucia .
Autre condition particulièrement importante : Jason et Lucia doivent tous les deux posséder le profil criminel Professionnel . Pour préserver ce statut, évitez autant que possible les actes de violence gratuits. Privilégiez les approches discrètes pendant les braquages, neutralisez les ennemis sans les tuer lorsque c’est possible et épargnez les personnages lorsque vous en avez l’occasion.
Attention, un personnage qui atteint le niveau Irrécupérable ne pourra plus revenir en arrière. Il est donc préférable de surveiller régulièrement votre profil, surtout si vous souhaitez obtenir la meilleure fin. Vous pouvez retrouver davantage de détails dans notre guide consacré aux profils criminels .
C’est probablement la condition la plus contraignante. Pour obtenir la meilleure fin, vous devrez avoir placé 2 000 000 $ dans l’épargne familiale de Jason et Lucia . Attention, nous parlons bien de l’argent transféré sur le compte d’épargne familial dans l’application BuckMe. Les sommes conservées sur votre compte courant ou dans vos poches ne sont pas prises en compte.
Vous pouvez alimenter ce compte progressivement tout au long de votre aventure. Nous vous recommandons d’ailleurs de commencer assez tôt, notamment grâce aux revenus des braquages, des activités secondaires et de la revente de marchandises. Une fois l’argent versé dans l’épargne familiale, vous ne pourrez plus le récupérer librement. En revanche, il sera conservé jusqu’au dénouement.
Une fois les trois conditions précédentes réunies, vous pouvez commencer la mission « Garde préventive », dans le chapitre 5. Lorsque le jeu vous propose de poursuivre ou de reporter le dénouement avant votre rendez-vous avec Abe, assurez-vous d’avoir atteint les objectifs précédents. Dans le cas contraire, mieux vaut repousser la mission et retourner en exploration libre.

articles.chapeau: Un prototype multijoueur pirate de GTA 6 fait déjà circuler voitures et voix sur PC à 25–30 fps. Entre portage non officiel, DMCA et malwares, la partie devient risquée.
articles.txt:
Un prototype multijoueur pirate de GTA 6 fait déjà circuler voitures et voix sur PC à 25–30 fps. Entre portage non officiel, DMCA et malwares, la partie devient risquée.
Un multijoueur de GTA 6 tournant sur PC à 25-30 fps, avec voitures et chat vocal de proximité : c’est ce que montre un prototype privé qui affole déjà les fans de GTA 6 Online .
Alors que Rockstar Games n’a toujours annoncé ni version PC ni mode en ligne pour Grand Theft Auto VI , un petit groupe de moddeurs affirme avoir fait fonctionner un début de multi sur un portage PC non officiel . Mais que vaut vraiment cette « première » et qu’est-ce que cela change pour les joueurs PC en attente d’une sortie officielle de GTA 6 Online ?
Le projet est suivi via PortWatch VI , un site communautaire qui suit l’avancée des différents ports pirates de GTA 6 . Il crédite déjà certains builds solo comme Belobug à 91,3 % avec environ 22 fps, mais uniquement sur les machines des développeurs.
Dans une mise à jour relayée par GamesRadar, PortWatch affirme que « GTA 6 multiplayer is running on PC ». Selon la plateforme, « TeK’s group has players, cars and proximity voice chat working at a stable 25 to 30 fps, on a private fork of CGBJ’s build » et « PortWatch has verified the video is real ».
Derrière ce prototype, on trouve le moddeur TeKGameR950 , qui exploite une branche privée du port CGBJ , lui-même basé sur une fuite de l’exécutable Xbox diffusée par le leaker Cyberleek . Jusqu’ici, tous les ports suivaient uniquement le solo : c’est la première fois qu’une vidéo montre personnages, véhicules et voix de proximité synchronisés entre plusieurs joueurs sur PC.
Techniquement, faire parler plusieurs copies de GTA 6 entre elles est un gros défi. Il faut que chaque instance du jeu soit d’accord sur la position de chaque joueur, de chaque voiture et sur les collisions, sans serveur central digne d’un vrai GTA 6 Online .
Les chiffres avancés – 25 à 30 fps – restent très loin d’un confort de jeu standard et ne concernent que la configuration exacte des développeurs. PortWatch rappelle aussi que « playable » signifie surtout que le personnage se déplace et que la mission démarre, pas que l’expérience ressemble à un produit fini.
Surtout, ce multijoueur de TeK reste entièrement privé . Aucun exécutable propre, aucun launcher, aucun serveur public n’est partagé. Pour le joueur lambda, il n’existe aujourd’hui aucune façon légale ou sûre de tester ce « GTA 6 multijoueur PC ».
Côté juridique, Take-Two Interactive a déjà dégainé le DMCA . L’éditeur a fait supprimer le projet Leonida et 3 007 dépôts GitHub liés aux ports de GTA 6 . Ce signal est clair : ces versions restent dans le viseur et leur diffusion publique serait rapidement coupée.
Côté sécurité, les chiffres sont tout aussi inquiétants. Kaspersky recense plus de 27 000 programmes malveillants se faisant passer pour des « GTA 6 PC » ou « GTA 6 Online ». Des kits d’arnaque « fake port PC » se vendraient même autour de 200 dollars (environ 185 €) sur le dark web. Les sites sérieux rappellent que tous les liens de téléchargement GTA 6 PC actuels sont à considérer comme suspects.
Officiellement, GTA 6 est sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S , uniquement en solo. Une rumeur évoque une version PC début 2027, mais Rockstar Games n’a rien confirmé, et GTA 6 Online n’a toujours pas de fenêtre de sortie.
À retenir : oui, un multijoueur pirate de GTA 6 semble tourner en labo sur PC, mais non, ce n’est pas le vrai GTA 6 Online, et non, vous ne pouvez pas y jouer sans prendre des risques sérieux, autant légaux que sécuritaires.

articles.txt:
Treize ans après un GTA V qui culmine aujourd’hui à plus de 230 millions d’unités vendues, Rockstar Games est de retour avec Grand Theft Auto VI et les attentes étaient tout simplement énormes. Chaque déclaration, image, fuite, bande-annonce et présentation ont été décortiquées dans tous les sens pour en savoir plus sur un titre qui restait malgré tout assez mystérieux. Le 18 novembre, l’embargo sur la presse est tombé et celle-ci a gratifié GTA 6 d’une note moyenne agrégée de 99 sur 100 sur le site Metacritic après plus de 150 tests publiés. Peu après la sortie, l’éditeur Take-Two a révélé que GTA 6 et les aventures criminelles de Jason et Lucia avaient généré 3,79 milliards de dollars avant sa sortie pour plus de 32,5 millions d’unités précommandées. C’est le plus gros lancement d’un produit culturel de toute l’histoire, tout simplement. Si vous souhaitez vous le procurer au meilleur prix sur PS5, voici les trois enseignes où il est affiché au meilleur prix.
Découvrez Vice City et l’État de Leonida pour 79,99 euros chez Auchan en profitant de la version boîte de GTA VI. Cette version propose donc une boîte PS5 contenant un code de téléchargement, mais également un poster réversible. En passant par Auchan, vous pourrez profiter du retrait en 1 h en magasin.
Chez Micromania, GTA VI est également affiché au prix de 79,99 euros dans sa version boîte sur PS5, mais vous tourner vers l’enseigne spécialisée vous permet, d’une part, de récupérer 800 points de fidélité sur votre carte et, d’autre part, de baisser le prix à 39,99 euros en revendant un jeu ou un accessoire figurant sur la liste des produits éligibles. Cliquez ici pour profiter de l’offre sur GTA 6
On termine avec E. Leclerc, qui affiche cette même version boîte de GTA VI sur PS5 au prix de 69,99 euros. Là encore, il s’agit d’une boîte de jeu contenant un code de téléchargement ainsi qu’un poster, mais vous profitez de la remise immédiate et d’une livraison offerte en Click&Collect.
Ce qu’il faut retenir sur GTA 6 : GTA 6 est un jeu d’action et d’aventure à la 3e personne en mode ouvert très vivant, plein d’activités, ultra-réaliste et d’une scénarisation très avancée. En histoire, secrets et découverte, GTA 6 vous immerge pleinement dans son univers.

articles.chapeau: Une vidéo promet GTA 6 à 180 images par seconde sur PC, en format ultra-large et avec ray tracing. Le compteur oublie simplement de préciser que cinq
articles.txt:
À en croire une séquence qui tourne sur X depuis le début d’après-midi, GTA 6 tournerait déjà six fois mieux sur un PC pirate que sur une PS5 Pro.
Son auteur, D Everett Hinton, affirme dans une vidéo publiée sur X atteindre 30 images par seconde natives, propulsées à 180 grâce à la génération d’images, le tout en HDR10+ avec un moteur graphique « entièrement réécrit ».
Il assure au passage que la plupart des autres extraits en ligne sont faux, contrairement au sien. Pourtant, son nom n’apparaît dans aucun des projets recensés par les sites qui suivent la course des portages , et pas une seule ligne de code n’a été publiée.
GTA 6 PC port with 5120×1440 32:9, 30fps (at 16:9) and 180fps with frame gen, HDR 10+, Nvidia Reflex, etc, with ray reconstruction and DLSS 5 NR coming soon.. most of the videos you see are fake, this one is not! Completely rewritten CPU/GPU pipeline. pic.twitter.com/OjZXboxqQH
Ce contenu est bloqué car vous n’avez pas accepté les cookies et autres traceurs. Ce contenu est fourni par Twitter. Pour pouvoir le visualiser, vous devez accepter l’usage étant opéré par Twitter avec vos données qui pourront être utilisées pour les finalités suivantes : vous permettre de visualiser et de partager des contenus avec des médias sociaux, favoriser le développement et l’amélioration des produits d’Humanoid et de ses partenaires, vous afficher des publicités personnalisées par rapport à votre profil et activité, vous définir un profil publicitaire personnalisé, mesurer la performance des publicités et du contenu de ce site et mesurer l’audience de ce site (en savoir plus)
En cliquant sur « J’accepte tout », vous consentez aux finalités susmentionnées pour l’ensemble des cookies et autres traceurs déposés par Humanoid et ses partenaires .
Vous gardez la possibilité de retirer votre consentement à tout moment. Pour plus d’informations, nous vous invitons à prendre connaissance de notre Politique cookies .
En regardant l’extrait de plus près, les zones d’ombre s’accumulent vite. La vidéo se limite au prologue de la prison, en intérieur, loin de la charge d’un monde ouvert ou d’une course-poursuite en voiture.
L’image est vendue comme du 32:9 (le format des écrans ultra-larges), mais elle tient en réalité dans un fichier 1080p encadré de bandes noires.
L’auteur reconnaît d’ailleurs lui-même que les 30 images par seconde sont mesurées en 16:9, et non dans la définition géante de 5 120 par 1 440 pixels. Quant au compteur affiché à l’écran, il est fait maison et n’indique ni la carte graphique ni le processeur utilisés.
Un détail technique vend immédiatement la mèche : le chiffre affiché vaut toujours exactement six fois la cadence réelle (30 donne 180, et 27,6 donne 165,6).
Ce ratio correspond au mode 6X du DLSS 4.5, qui demande aux cartes RTX 50 d’inventer cinq images intermédiaires pour chaque image réellement calculée.
Concrètement, le jeu continue de tourner à 30 images par seconde : la physique et la réactivité à la manette ne progressent pas d’un pouce. Nous avions déjà expliqué le grand paradoxe de la génération multi-images , qui gonfle spectaculairement les compteurs sans offrir la fluidité d’un vrai rendu natif.
Sans preuve formelle, l’hypothèse la plus crédible reste celle d’une simple capture de la version console à 30 images par seconde, passée ensuite à la moulinette de la génération d’images. La manipulation a d’ailleurs déjà été montrée mi-novembre avec une PS5 Pro reliée à un PC équipé d’une RTX 5090 pour afficher 180 images par seconde.
Ce n’est donc pas un montage grossier, puisque l’on voit bien GTA 6 , mais plutôt le mirage des 60 fps de cette semaine multiplié par trois.

Si l’on coupe la génération d’images pour regarder les mesures réelles, le tableau est beaucoup plus modeste.
Tous ces chiffres proviennent des auteurs ou de leurs testeurs (et restent à vérifier de manière indépendante), mais aucun projet n’approche encore les 30 images par seconde en monde ouvert :
Côté juridique, GitHub n’a publié aucun nouvel avis de retrait au nom de Take-Two depuis la vague de mardi (3 007 dépôts supprimés).
Selon la documentation de Vice-Tay, c’est l’auteur de CGBJ qui a choisi de retirer lui-même son projet, dont une branche privée sert de base à la démo multijoueur de jeudi soir .
Pour s’y retrouver dans cette course, le tableau des scores de PortWatch VI reste la meilleure boussole.

articles.t: Deux joueurs réunis dans GTA 6 sur PC grâce à un portage privé, avant la sortie officielle
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 PC : TeK montre deux joueurs connectés sur un portage privé et annonce 25 à 30 FPS. Le chat de proximité fonctionne aussi, d’après PortWatch VI.
articles.txt:
Deux personnages sur le tarmac d’un aéroport, une sportive rouge qui circule : la scène paraît banale, mais elle réunit des joueurs sur une version Windows encore non officielle. La démonstration franchit une nouvelle étape pour les projets communautaires, sans constituer pour autant un équivalent du service de Rockstar.
Le développeur TeK a publié sur X une courte vidéo montrant deux personnages présents dans la même session, dont l’un conduit une voiture sur la piste. Il affirme que cette version tient 25 à 30 FPS stables et prend également en charge le chat de proximité.
La séquence semble relativement fluide, mais aucun compteur d’images par seconde n’apparaît à l’écran. La configuration utilisée n’est pas précisée et le décor se limite essentiellement à une piste vide : ces conditions ne permettent pas d’extrapoler les performances à une circulation dense ou à une session plus chargée.
Le site communautaire PortWatch VI , qui suit ces projets de portage, a vérifié indépendamment l’authenticité de la vidéo. Il confirme aussi le fonctionnement du chat de proximité, mais ne valide pas les chiffres de performances avancés par TeK.
D’après PortWatch VI, le groupe de TeK travaille sur un fork privé de la build CGBJ , elle-même fondée sur les projets open source VIctory et XCL. Le code n’est pas public à ce stade : les autres développeurs et les joueurs ne peuvent donc pas reproduire librement cette démonstration.
Ces travaux s’inscrivent dans une progression rapide des recompilations communautaires, dont une grande partie du travail repose sur des modèles d’IA, selon TechPowerUp. Le média rapportait la veille que certains projets atteignaient 20 FPS en jeu , tandis que d’autres équipes revendiquaient déjà des résultats supérieurs.
La démonstration intervient alors que des informations antérieures évoquaient une version PC officielle au premier trimestre 2027 et un lancement de GTA VI Online en 2027. Elle ne renseigne toutefois ni sur les fonctionnalités prévues par Rockstar, ni sur une éventuelle évolution de ses plans ou de ceux de Take-Two Interactive.
Faire coexister deux joueurs et transmettre leur voix constitue une avancée technique, mais ne démontre pas la capacité à gérer des sessions nombreuses, la persistance ou la stabilité d’un service en ligne. Pour les joueurs, cette vidéo reste donc une démonstration, pas une version à installer : des téléchargements présentés comme des portages non officiels de GTA 6 sur PC ont déjà servi à dissimuler des logiciels malveillants.

articles.txt:
A 208.62GB GTA 6 repack on a Russian torrent site uses VIctory to run a leaked Xbox Series X|S build on Windows, not a native PC version. Reported performance is poor and inconsistent, and the anonymous download poses a security risk; its claims lack reliable benchmarks.

GTA 6 has been out on PS5 and Xbox for about a week, and a supposed PC version has now appeared on a Russian torrent site. According to HKEPC , a 208.62GB repack labeled as a GTA 6 "Recomp" for PC showed up on the file-sharing site Rutor on November 26. It is marked as version 1.0.2.1, claims to be portable with no installation required, and uses the VIctory runtime.
As we covered before , this isn't a native PC build from Rockstar. VIctory is an open-source compatibility layer that runs the leaked Xbox Series X|S build on Windows. It executes the game's x86-64 code directly, replaces the Xbox system software, and translates the console's shaders for DirectX 12.
The file size also lines up with the leaked Xbox package, which is roughly 209GB. The recomp label is a little misleading, too, as most of these projects rely on compatibility and translation layers rather than true static recompilation. The torrent listing claims the following system requirements:
Performance reports are all over the place. Reddit users who claim to have tried the repack report between 10 and 30 FPS on systems with 32GB of RAM and 16GB of VRAM. Even then, they describe very low rendering resolutions, overly dark visuals, and missing or flickering textures.
Another claim circulating in a Reddit thread suggests the game can reach 30 FPS on an RTX 4070. That's unverified, and the RTX 4070 has 12GB of VRAM, below the listing's own stated 16GB minimum, so take that claim with a grain of salt.
2 PortWatch VI tracks unofficial efforts to run the leaked Xbox Series X|S build of GTA 6 on PC. VIEW GALLERY - 2 IMAGES These figures are also considerably higher than the 3 to 5 FPS reported for the best-known PortWatch VI forks. The difference could come down to a newer build, different hardware, or lower rendering settings, but there's no reliable benchmark to establish how well this particular repack performs.
Interestingly, several reddit comments vouched for the moderation on Russian torrent trackers, saying they'd never had problems downloading from them. One user who tried an earlier port said it ran at around 4 FPS and took two hours to finish the first mission. One of the most upvoted replies even argued that Rockstar deserved this for delaying the PC release.
However, despite the endorsements, we'd strongly advise against downloading this repack. A 200GB file from an anonymous uploader is a considerable security risk, particularly when fake cracked PC versions of GTA 6 are already circulating.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC Port Takes a Massive Leap Forward in Just Days
articles.chapeau: We got GTA 6 multiplayer on PC before we got GTA 6's official release on PC
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games finally released Grand Theft Auto 6 this month after fans had waited 13 years . Unfortunately, PC players are still waiting as no PC port has been officially announced . But following the catastrophic leak of an apparent build of the game onto the internet, PC players have begun a race to create an unofficial version of GTA 6 . That race started slowly, but progress has been exponential in only a few days.
If you followed the news in the lead-up to GTA 6 's release, then you are probably familiar with the name Cyberleek . The prolific hacker raised millions of dollars in cryptocurrency by sharing unauthorized clips of Rockstar's big release ahead of launch. With the game now available​​​​​​​ to the public, it seemed like Cyberleek's time in the spotlight might be over. That proved to be untrue on Nov. 23, when Cyberleek released an apparent Xbox executable file that serves as a goldmine for programmers, hackers, and emulation enthusiasts, allowing them to start the hard work of making an unofficial PC port of GTA 6 a reality​​​​​​​.
In the first hours after the build went public, multiple projects posted early builds that could get the game running​​​​​​​ . It was not in a playable state, however, with incomplete shaders and models and extremely low frame rates​​​​​​​ . Now, only a handful of days later, new updates are showing the game in a much better state. Progress on the various builds is constantly documented on sites like Reddit and PortWatch VI ​​​​​​​ . The latest footage shows that GTA 6 is now actually playable on PC, though not completely. Videos of the game's opening missions are common now, with models fully rendered. One Reddit user showed​​​​​​​ that they had gotten the XCL port (one of the more prominent forks) running at over 30 fps, a pretty respectable, stable frame rate​​​​​​​ . The leading build on PortWatch VI, from Belobug, is currently said to be over 90% playable.
This speedy progress is largely the result of generative AI's newfound impact on the hacking scene . The process of decompiling and building a port of a game previously took months and even years to complete, but that can now be done in hours with the right tools. This is often called vibe-coding, which has produced mixed results in similar projects.​​​​​​​ Even Xbox is getting in on the technology, announcing the Xbox Labs division , which CEO Asha Sharma described as "a small group of game makers​​​​​​​ , engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience."
With swift progress on an unofficial GTA 6 PC port, teams are starting to go beyond replicating the console experience. X user TeK posted a video showing​​​​​​​ multiplayer running on a fork of the CGBJ build. articles.t: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
articles.chapeau: More than 40 projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 to PC through reverse engineering just days after its $3.79 billion record console launch. AI coding agents like Claude Code are speeding up the process so much that an early unofficial multiplayer mode is already running. Rockstar's delayed PC business model is coming under pressure.
articles.txt:
Easy Perspectives Terms Own question Key Points Following a leak, developers are porting GTA 6 to PC through reverse engineering. They are using AI coding tools to speed up the work. Tracking data shows rapid progress across dozens of projects. Some already boot the game and show early multiplayer features. The unofficial builds threaten Rockstar's business model, while legal action against decentralized groups has little effect. Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model.
A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek distributed a stolen Xbox image of the game, and the executable itself leaked a few days ago.
Since then, a fast-moving scene of developers and modders has sprung up to get the game running on Windows through reverse engineering, compatibility layers, and recompilation. AI coding tools like Anthropic's Claude Code are driving that pace. Instead of spending months manually analyzing code and rebuilding console functions, developers are handing off much of the porting work to AI agents. One group even livestreamed the process.
A tracking platform lists 40 active projects less than four days after the executable leaked. Nearly half of them can boot the game on PC. On the platform's own rating scale, the furthest project is more than 90 percent of the way to a playable PC build.
Some projects are trying to add features including native ray-traced lighting. Gameplay footage of an unofficial PC multiplayer mode surfaced on November 26, and the platform's operator verified it. It shows multiple players moving through the game world with vehicles and voice chat at 25 to 30 frames per second. GTA 6 has officially launched only as a single-player title, and an online mode has no release date yet.
There is no finished PC version ready for the general public yet. The most stable builds are incomplete, circulate in closed groups, or require substantial technical know-how. Even so, this pace breaks a decades-old assumption in the gaming industry. Console emulators often took years after a hardware generation launched, and brand-new blockbusters rarely ran on them soon after release.
Rockstar and parent company Take-Two face more than a technical nuisance. The studio traditionally releases its flagship games on consoles first and follows with PC versions much later. GTA V took about 19 months to reach PC, and Red Dead Redemption 2 took about a year. So far, there is no official PC release date for GTA 6. That approach cuts optimization work at launch and encourages impatient players to buy the game twice.
The online business is an even bigger vulnerability. Nearly 80 percent of Take-Two's total revenue in fiscal year 2026 came from microtransactions and recurring digital spending. GTA Online alone has brought in more than $5 billion so far. A free, community-run PC multiplayer mode targets that financial backbone before Rockstar has even launched its own version.
Past experience with FiveM for GTA V shows how nervous Take-Two is about parallel worlds like this. In 2015, the company cracked down hard on the alternative multiplayer and roleplay mod. It banned developer accounts and, according to some developers, even sent private investigators to the creators' homes to shut down the project .
FiveM grew into the core of the roleplay scene despite that pushback and at times drew more concurrent players on Steam than the base game. Only then did Rockstar reverse course and acquire the development team Cfx.re in August 2023. Back then, the community needed years to build a parallel ecosystem like that. For GTA 6, an early PC multiplayer prototype has surfaced just a week after launch.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaked Xbox Build Boots on Windows at 1 FPS
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek released the missing GTA 6 executable. The VIctory project says the leaked Xbox build boots on Windows, but the world runs at about 1 FPS.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Cyberleek, the name reporters use for the anonymous leaker behind the leaked 209GB GTA 6 Xbox build , released the missing executable on 23 November 2026. An open source project called VIctory now says the game boots on Windows. According to Make Tech Easier and NoobFeed, the project’s README describes menus running at 30 FPS and the game world running at approximately 1 FPS. Nobody would call that playable.
The number reads like a failure, but it works better as a progress marker. A leaked console build that reaches the prologue on a PC is a real step for the unofficial porting scene. An earlier VIctory fork test on different hardware also landed in single-digit frame rates, which we covered in our report on the VIctory fork running GTA 6 at 3 FPS . The new claim moves the needle only slightly on speed, yet it changes the story on whether the files can start at all.
Every claim here comes with a caveat. Reporting describes the files as an alleged Xbox build, not an officially released product. The 209GB size traces to Cyberleek’s own claim. Reports also say the Windows boot, the prologue access and the frame rates have not been independently verified. This analysis separates what outlets reported from what anyone has actually confirmed, and it explains why the gap between the two matters for players, for Rockstar Games and for the wider modding community.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
The core news is narrow. Reports date the release of the missing executable to 23 November 2026. That file completed a package that had been circulating since 19 November without it. Without an executable, a build is a pile of data. With one, a technical community can at least try to launch it, which is exactly what happened within days.
The Cyberleek GTA 6 executable matters because of what it signals about the leak’s structure. Console builds ship as a set of assets, engine libraries and a main binary that ties them together. Release only the first two and the community can browse textures, audio and scripts, but it cannot watch anything run. Release the binary and the question changes from what is inside to whether it moves.
Reports tie the leaked material to Rockstar Games and to files from its RAGE engine. They also describe the archive as an Xbox version, not a retail PC product. That distinction frames everything that follows. A PC cannot run an Xbox binary natively, so any boot on Windows implies translation work rather than a simple double-click.
Cyberleek remains a label rather than a person. Reporting identifies no individual, and this article does not suggest otherwise. Readers should treat the name as shorthand for whoever posted the archive and the executable, nothing more.
Related guides: From the same topic area, our evergreen pick is PS5 Pro vs Xbox Series X , a page we keep current rather than a story that dates; the Shattered guides hub groups it with the other setup guides and comparisons we maintain, each listed with a one-line description written for it.
The sequence is short, and the dates come straight from the reporting. The build appeared first, minus its executable. Four days later the executable followed. Then the open source side moved quickly. Our own earlier coverage of the executable leak and the missing playable PC build captured the mood before the boot claims arrived, when the community had a binary in hand but no proof it could run.
Look at the last column. Not one row in that table carries a confirmation from Rockstar or from a neutral technical reviewer. The story rests on a leaker’s word, a project’s README and a handful of outlets relaying both. That is enough to report, but not enough to treat as settled fact.
VIctory is the open source project at the center of the story. Reports say its README makes three specific claims. The game boots. It reaches the prologue. Menus run at 30 FPS, while the game world runs at approximately 1 FPS. The project itself labels that last result as unplayable.
That honesty deserves credit. Plenty of leak-adjacent projects oversell their progress with cropped clips and vague promises. A README that states a 1 FPS world figure and calls it not playable gives other developers a concrete baseline. It also sets expectations for the many readers who hear boots on Windows and assume a working PC version is days away.

articles.t: Vibecoding Teen Behind Nuked GTA 6 PC Port Project 'Leonida' Vows to Continue, Says Parents 'Have Warned Me About What Could Happen'
articles.chapeau: The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
articles.txt:
The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
‘NotRexed’ is behind ‘Project Leonida,’ which was at one point leading the race to create a PC port of GTA 6 following the recent leak of an Xbox build. Cyberleek, the infamous leaker behind many early GTA 6 gameplay clips, reportedly released the Xbox build of GTA 6 last week, and vibecoders have been attempting to port the game to PC since.
Fueled by AI, progress has been swift, with clips showing GTA 6 running on PC at a higher frame rate than on console, and one video even showing basic multiplayer. Obviously, Rockstar Games, which will no doubt release GTA 6 on PC officially at some point, and parent company Take-Two will be watching the homebrew scene’s every move like a hawk.
In the case of Project Leonida, Take-Two has already taken action. NotRexed was organizing and sharing work on a Discord group, and hosting their findings on a GitHub repository, when cease and desists from Take-Two hauled everything offline. NotRexed then took to social media to announce they'd decided to call it a day.
“I quit guys. I’m sorry,” NotRexed said. “I really want to make cool stuff but every single time s**t happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the Discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.”
NotRexed went on to insist that they were finding it tough to run Project Leonida while also going to school. “Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid,” they said. “Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.”
However, NotRexed has now returned, and promised to continue the project. “Ignore my other posts,” NotRexed said after changing their mind. “Something’s coming soon. Leonida is NOT dead. I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I’ll have some stuff to show all of you soon.”
IGN spoke to NotRexed to find out why they’re doing this, whether they understand the risks, what they’ll do if they get in legal trouble, and what their parents think of it all.
“It’s just a hobby of mine,” NotRexed said in a private message. “I started doing similar things with porting games to the web back in the start of 2026, and I’ve always just thought of it to be cool.”
Before generative AI, NotRexed had no interest in porting games to other platforms, they said. But after finding out it was possible in 2025, they’re now taking on one of the most powerful publishers in video games. Interestingly, there’s no real motive behind it.
“I’ve always been interested in tech and mess around with it a lot,” they said. According to them, even their parents are aware of what they do and are largely supportive of it. “Yes, they know about all my projects and work I do, and they’re pretty encouraging about it,” they claimed.
It made me wonder if they were fully aware of the legal risks involved in such an undertaking. “Yea, they have warned me about what could happen,” NotRexed insisted when I asked if their parents knew about the potential legal issues. “I’m still continuing my work as of now tho because even tho T2 took down my repo and Discord they have never sent an email or message directly to me. If I do get into legal trouble I’m probably gonna stop working on it but possibly have a friend continue it.”
How feasible is this? IGN asked Matt Freedman, a veteran game developer with expertise in both traditional development and the controversial emerging technology of AI.
“A recompilation is different from a port,” Freedman said. “But yes, an AI driven recompilation of GTA 6 is very doable and wouldn't have the same 'game feel' problems that an AI-driven port would have.”
He went on to explain the differences between decompilations, recompilations, and ports. A decomp is where someone manually reverse engineers a game to run on other systems, like the Mario 64 PC port. “This is very time consuming and requires a human to do the work and effectively 'guess' how the game works,” he said.
A port takes existing assets or creates new ones and essentially builds a new version of the same game to work on another system. The Witcher 3’s Switch port is an example of this. “A team took The Witcher 3 code base and assets and then modified them by hand to work on the Switch,” he said.

articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A deleted Pastebin document attributed to GTAForums dataminer Tex2 reportedly lists GTA 6 graphics settings for four consoles. KitGuru reported that the deleted leak may have revealed Rockstar’s graphics settings for the PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Rockstar Games has not confirmed any of it.
MP1st, The Times of India, iXBT.games and GamesRadar+ also carried the story, which kept it circulating on November 27, 2026. The document is gone, so readers cannot check the original page. That gap matters, and this analysis treats every detail as a report, not as a fact about the shipping game.
The timing adds fuel. Players are still debating what a possible PC version could look like, a thread we followed in our report on the GTA 6 leak for PC gamers and its November build . A console settings list gives that debate new material, even if it proves nothing about PC.

The core claim is simple. A Pastebin document, since deleted, reportedly carried graphics presets for the PS5, PS5 Pro , Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of Grand Theft Auto VI. It did not leak a build, a trailer or a story detail. It leaked a settings list, the kind of data a developer keeps in internal config files or debug menus.
According to the reports, the list covered texture quality, shadow quality, terrain detail, hair quality, global illumination, NPC behavior, pedestrian density and physics quality. Those eight areas span both rendering and simulation. Some tax the GPU, others tax the CPU, and a few hit both. A preset that touches all of them tells you how a studio balances the whole machine, not only the pretty parts.
The presence of NPC behavior, pedestrian density and physics quality stands out. Those options suggest the document describes the full game simulation and not just the visual layer. Open-world games live and die by how many people, cars and objects the engine can keep alive at once, so the CPU side of the list may matter as much as the shadows.
Nothing in the available coverage supplies resolution targets, frame rates or a full value-by-value table that we can verify. Outlets described the document in broad strokes, and we do the same. Any site that prints a complete table of exact values is working from a page that no longer exists.
Related guides: From the same topic area, our evergreen pick is PS5 Pro vs PS5 , a page we keep current rather than a story that dates; the Shattered guides hub groups it with the other setup guides and comparisons we maintain, each listed with a one-line description written for it.
Reports attribute the Pastebin to Tex2, a member of GTAForums who is described as a dataminer. Dataminers pull information out of game files, patches and builds. Their track records vary widely, and the strongest ones show their work. A deleted paste with no surviving original shows very little.
The attribution itself comes secondhand. Outlets repeat the name because earlier posts and forum threads pointed to it, and not because anyone has proven who posted the paste. Rockstar has not said whether the document is authentic, whether it came from a current build or whether it reflects an older internal state.
Journalists use a rough ladder for leaks. The top rung is a document the publisher confirms. The next is material several independent outlets inspected directly. The bottom rung is a description of something nobody can open any more. This story sits near the bottom, which is why the fact pattern stays modest: four platforms, a few named features and no official word.

articles.t: GTA 6 release produces rash of bricked Xbox consoles, joining failing PS5s
articles.chapeau: Following the GTA 6 launch, bricked Xbox consoles are appearing in droves at service centers. A Polish technician examined Xbox Series X and S units that won’t turn on or crash repeatedly. PS5s have also suffered from apparent overheating issues, exposed by the demanding Rockstar title.
articles.txt:
Instances of dying or dead PS5 consoles have risen since the GTA 6 release date . However, the Xbox Series X and S are not immune to problems when exploring the Leonida map . A repair shop reported an unusually high rate of catastrophic failures for Microsoft’s hardware.
Technician modyfikatorcasper noted that in Poland, Xbox consoles are much less prevalent than their PlayStation rivals. Regardless, they now represent 2 out of 10 systems sent to the company for service. The number of units with issues has increased sharply compared to previous months.
Symptoms include random shutdowns or crashes during GTA 6 gameplay . Other gaming machines have slowed to a crawl or refuse to install updates. In the worst scenarios, a bricked Xbox Series X either won’t power on or output a blank video signal.
The launch of the Rockstar title boosted PS5 and Xbox console sales , while other players may have activated dormant systems. As a result, it’s not surprising modyfikatorcasper would experience a massive uptick in requests. Nevertheless, support subreddits indicate the severe issues aren’t entirely isolated.
Poster Top_Nothing_3145 initially avoided trouble and completed a long gameplay session. Unfortunately, the Series X wouldn't turn on the next morning. Evidence points to a dead power supply, with some readers recommending replacing the component.
Redditor Jastafool could only play the GTA 6 Xbox version for 10 minutes before the fun came to a halt. A local fix-it shop believes a faulty motherboard is causing the startup failure, rather than the PSU.
The less serious cases involve frequent crashes to the dashboard that prevent progress. Rockstar released a patch on November 23rd to address these reports, but it didn’t resolve them for many gamers.
Modyfikatorcasper found that in ailing PS5s, the infamous liquid metal leak is often the culprit. What’s plaguing the Microsoft machines is more debatable, though overheating is again suspected. The diagnostic process is less defined for the Xbox Series X and S, forcing the technician to develop custom tools.
The GTA 6 Xbox and PS5 versions may not be pushing the hardware past their designed limits. Still, the bricked consoles suggest the game is, at minimum, dealing a death blow to already problematic units.

articles.t: GTA 6 Metacritic User Score: 5.6 vs 99 Critics
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 Metacritic user score sits near 5.6 while critics give a 99 Metascore from 152 reviews. Here is what the numbers and outlets confirm.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Rockstar Games shipped Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, and Metacritic now shows two very different verdicts. Critics gave it a 99 Metascore from 152 reviews, while the user score sits at 5.7 from 116,374 ratings . That works out to a 42-point gap once you put both numbers on the same 100-point scale.
The GTA 6 Metacritic user score has become the loudest argument in gaming this week. Some outlets call it review bombing. Others say players have real complaints and deserve a hearing. Our earlier piece on how GTA VI tied Ocarina of Time at 99 covered the critic side. This analysis covers the other half of the ledger, using only figures that named outlets reported and that Metacritic’s own listing confirms.
One caution before the details. The confirmed numbers show that the gap exists. They do not prove why it exists. No study, no Rockstar statement and no Metacritic announcement has established a single cause, so this article separates what the data shows from what outlets infer.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with the critic side. Metacritic lists Grand Theft Auto VI, published by Rockstar Games, at a 99 Metascore built from 152 critic reviews. That score matches the all-time high that Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time has held for years. Yahoo’s entertainment desk, in a November 21 report by Marvin Montanaro , noted that IGN, GameSpot and Eurogamer all awarded perfect scores. Eurogamer’s own review called the game an open world of “awe, minute detail and impossible scale.”
Now the player side. Metacritic’s current listing shows a 5.7 user score from 116,374 ratings. On November 21, outlets reported 5.6 from 53,044 ratings. Eurogamer, writing the same day , described the figure as 5.6 out of 10 and said Metacritic classifies it as “mixed or average.” So the average climbed one tenth of a point while the sample more than doubled.
The 42-point gap is our arithmetic, not a figure Metacritic publishes. We multiplied the 5.7 user score by ten to match the critic scale. It gives readers a fast way to see how far apart the two groups sit.
The user score did not start at 5.6. Yahoo reported that earlier observations put the audience score in the 3 to 4 range before it began recovering. Eurogamer said the score “had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.” Both outlets are describing the same pattern. Yahoo offered three possible reasons for the climb: genuine positive feedback, removal of suspicious ratings, or other shifts in who was rating.
That recovery matters for how you read any single screenshot. A score captured on launch night says little about the final picture. A score captured after 100,000 ratings says more, though even that remains a live average that shifts by the hour.
Between the November 21 snapshot and the current listing, the sample grew by 63,330 ratings. The score barely moved. That stability suggests the average has settled into a band rather than swinging wildly, which is useful for anyone trying to judge whether the early zeros were a spike or a trend.
It also means the large sample cuts against a pure “small group of trolls” explanation. A group of tens of thousands can still be coordinated, but the numbers alone cannot tell us that. The Tribune piece reported that 43 percent of ratings were negative at 101,402 ratings. A coordinated campaign would have to be very large to produce that share.
Critic scores behave differently from user scores. A reviewer gets a copy before launch, plays a defined portion or all of the game, and files a score under an editor’s eye. The 152 reviews behind the 99 Metascore came from outlets that put their names on the work. Eurogamer’s five-star review is one example, and Yahoo listed IGN and GameSpot as other perfect-score awards.
That process produces tight clusters. When 152 professional reviews average 99, almost every one of them sits at the top of the scale. The aggregator has little spread to work with, which is why a handful of lower scores would barely move the number, and why the score has stayed put.
User scores work the other way. Every account counts the same, whether the player finished the 60-hour story, bounced off after two hours or never bought the game. Eurogamer’s reporter noted that some of the negative reviews raise genuine complaints while others do not. Both kinds of revie

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : pourquoi cette fuite PS5 et Xbox inquiète pour votre carte graphique — Frandroid
articles.chapeau: Des fichiers issus de GTA 6 révèlent les réglages graphiques de la PS5 et des Xbox. En croisant la fuite avec les analyses de Digital Foundry, elle donne
articles.txt:
D’après le dataminer Tex2, qui a fouillé les fichiers du jeu, et le site MP1st qui a relayé sa liste ce mercredi 25 novembre, la PS5 et la Xbox Series X utiliseraient les mêmes réglages, surtout en « moyen » et « élevé ». La PS5 Pro ajoute des ombres calculées en ray tracing, ce que Rockstar a confirmé, tandis que la Xbox Series S baisserait la qualité des textures et réduirait même la foule dans les rues. Nous avons détaillé cette fuite ici . Rockstar n’a pas commenté le reste de la liste.
Pour un PC, la conséquence est simple : les cartes graphiques de notre guide de configuration visent ces réglages de console. Pour jouer avec une image plus belle que sur PS5, il faudra davantage de puissance.
Pour l’instant, GTA 6 n’existe que sur PS5 et Xbox Series, où il est sorti le 19 novembre. Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune version PC, mais GamesBeat affirme, sur la foi de quatre sources anonymes, qu’elle est prévue pour le premier trimestre 2027 ; le studio n’a pas commenté. Ce serait bien plus rapide que pour GTA 5 , arrivé sur PC en avril 2015, soit environ un an et sept mois après sa sortie sur PS3 et Xbox 360.
L’information la plus solide vient de Digital Foundry , qui a comparé le jeu sur les quatre consoles. Toutes utilisent le ray tracing, une technique qui simule le trajet de la lumière, pour l’éclairage et les reflets. Même la Xbox Series S, la moins puissante , le conserve, quitte à calculer son image en 720p et à passer souvent sous les 30 images par seconde.
Aucune console ne permet de couper le ray tracing. Cela ne dit pas encore ce que proposera la version PC.
C’est un problème pour les PC équipés d’une carte sans circuits dédiés au ray tracing : GeForce GTX (séries 900, 10 et 16), Radeon RX 500 et RX 5000. Elles représentent encore plus de 13 % des PC du sondage Steam d’octobre 2026 . Certaines GTX savent faire du ray tracing grâce à leur pilote, sans circuits dédiés, mais rien ne garantit qu’elles seraient acceptées par GTA 6, ni assez rapides.
Je passe chez Apple ! Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Trois scénarios sont possibles, sans qu’on sache lequel Rockstar choisira.
Des circuits de ray tracing obligatoires. Ces cartes seraient alors exclues. C’est le choix d’ Indiana Jones et le Cercle ancien et de Doom: The Dark Ages , qui exigent une carte équipée pour le ray tracing.
Un ray tracing logiciel. Comme dans Star Wars Outlaws ou Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora , le jeu calcule alors le ray tracing sans circuits dédiés, et se lance donc sur ces cartes. Dans les tests de TechPowerUp en 1080p, une Radeon RX 5700 XT y fait jeu égal avec une RX 6600, équipée pour le ray tracing, alors qu’elle la devance d’environ 10 % dans les jeux sans ray tracing.
Un mode PC sans ray tracing. Rockstar l’a fait pour GTA 5 Enhanced, la version modernisée de GTA 5 sur PC : le ray tracing y est facultatif, et une GeForce GTX 1630 suffit au minimum.
Si un tel mode existait, le gain pourrait être important. Dans un test de GTA 5 Enhanced réalisé par le site polonais PurePC , activer le ray tracing fait perdre de 41 à 57 % des images par seconde en 1080p sur ces cartes courantes :
Sur 36 jeux testés en 4K, TechSpot mesure une perte moyenne plus modérée : de 22 à 32 % sur une GeForce RTX 4090, de 29 à 42 % sur une Radeon RX 7900 XTX, selon le niveau de ray tracing.
Ces mesures restent à prendre avec précaution, car GTA 5 est un jeu de 2013 auquel le ray tracing a été ajouté après coup, et PurePC ne l’a testé que sur une seule scène. Elles ne disent pas ce que gagnerait GTA 6 .
Digital Foundry juge d’ailleurs l’éclairage en ray tracing de GTA 5 Enhanced relativement léger pour la carte graphique, mais lourd pour le processeur. Enfin, notre guide suppose le ray tracing activé, comme sur console : ces gains ne s’appliquent pas à ses recommandations.
Avec les calculs de notre dossier , voici ce que donneraient des réglages au plus bas sur trois cartes graphiques très répandues. Ces projections reposent sur des gains mesurés dans d’autres jeux, souvent sur des cartes haut de gamme : ce ne sont que des ordres de grandeur.
En « bas », avec le ray tracing. Dans Red Dead Redemption 2 , du même moteur, ces réglages rapportent environ 13 à 26 % d’images par seco

Sur console, GTA 6 n’affiche aucun menu graphique : le jeu de Rockstar, sorti le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series, tourne à 30 images par seconde partout, sans dire ce que chaque machine sacrifie.
Un dataminer surnommé Tex2, qui fouille les fichiers du jeu, a trouvé la liste de ces réglages console par console. Son message sur le forum GTAForums a été supprimé depuis, mais le site MP1st l’a recopié ce mercredi 25 novembre .
La TV Micro RGB 65 » R95H à 1 999€ Black Friday : la TV Samsung Micro RGB 65″ R95H perd 1 000 € et s’affiche à 1 999 € au lieu de 2 999 €, du 21 au 30 novembre. Grâce à sa technologie Micro RGB, il délivre « un niveau de précision et de richesse colorimétrique inédit ».
Premier enseignement : la PS5 et la Xbox Series X utilisent exactement les mêmes réglages. Si la Xbox Series X tient mieux ses 30 images par seconde que la PS5 , la différence vient donc du matériel.
La PS5 Pro est la seule console à calculer les ombres en ray tracing, une technique qui simule le trajet de la lumière pour des ombres plus réalistes. Elle passe aussi l’éclairage global, c’est-à-dire la façon dont la lumière rebondit sur les surfaces, en « High » au lieu de « Medium ».
Pourtant, elle reste bloquée à 30 images par seconde, et aucun mode sans ray tracing ne permet d’échanger ces effets contre de la fluidité. Rockstar l’a justifié par le processeur de la PS5 Pro, trop juste pour faire tourner la simulation du jeu plus vite. Et comme la PS5 et la Series X mélangent déjà réglages moyens et élevés, un mode 60 images par seconde obligerait à les baisser encore , avec une image nettement moins belle.
La Xbox Series S, la moins puissante des quatre consoles, coupe plus large : textures, cheveux et eau perdent un cran. Surtout, la densité de piétons et de voitures passe de « High » à « Medium », comme la physique et le comportement des personnages.
Rockstar n’a toujours pas daté la version PC de GTA 6. En attendant, ces réglages donnent un repère pour estimer la configuration PC nécessaire pour faire tourner GTA 6 à 30 ou 60 images par seconde .

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Threads Email Instagram Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Extremely fast progress is being made with unofficial ports of GTA 6 One of those efforts runs at a stable 25 to 30fps now, but this requires 16GB of video RAM currently That's worrying those who have a graphics card with 12GB or 8GB of VRAM, but this is still very early days for these ports The rapid progress of unofficial PC ports of GTA 6 in the past 24 hours has been incredible to see unfold — but at the same time, what's been aired about the related PC specs for these projects is causing some concern with gamers.
And not just gamers who may be planning to run such an (illegal) unofficial port, but also those thinking about what the system requirements may be for Rockstar's official PC release.
The key info here comes from the 'CGBJ' build which has shared footage of GTA 6 running at a stable 25 to 30fps on PC as I reported earlier today . This port is currently hitting that frame rate on a PC with 8GB of system RAM and an Nvidia GPU that has 16GB of video memory (VRAM), and it's the latter point which is causing some concern.
Brackz on X , who highlighted this progress with the CGBJ project, asked their followers: "Seems like we might be seeing complete builds this weekend, will you be playing?"
And while some gamers do want to play — regardless of any risks associated with an illegal port, and that includes the danger of downloading a fake PC version that's malware in disguise, which are already around incidentally — they're quite worried about that 16GB of VRAM figure. Not many folks have a graphics card with this much memory on board, after all.
Is this really a concern, though – and more broadly, is it any kind of ominous sign for those planning to buy the official version of GTA 6 when Rockstar makes it available?
Well, I certainly wouldn't get carried away with the notion that seeing 16GB of VRAM mentioned in an unofficial port should be any cause for panic at this stage. Mind you, some folks are doing exactly that – panicking – along the lines of : "I hope they optimize it for 8GB VRAM too my broke ass can't afford the 16GB VRAM of AMD and Nvidia sadly."

That's the kind of level that PC gamers are anticipating for the official port from Rockstar, I should note — starting from 8GB of VRAM for 1080p (as the minimum spec) — although this is all guesswork.
